correctness.rationale: Closed form cross-checked against Eulerian recurrence; correction -(n+1)2^n vanishes at precisely the claimed eventual starting threshold. The same-parity two-adic difference has valuation exactly that of the half-index difference because the triangular difference is an odd multiple and the 9^t difference is eightfold more divisible. This gives one bijection on each parity, exact two-fiber counts, least period and sharp failure at the preceding index. Includes k=1..4. Finite checker matches 398 recurrence rows, 36 complete blocks and 15,288 valuation tests. The proof, not the experiments, establishes all k.

originality.rationale: The explicit Eulerian formula is known, but the consulted primary mathematical statements and sequence database do not give the full one-per-parity residue-fiber law at every two-power or the exact preperiod. Cao-Pan addresses fixed-row column sums, Nakamura fixed-size descent distributions, and Castro-Gonzalez-Medina described zero valuations (full text not accessible). Own previously recorded claims on Stirling, Stern, necklace and other sequences do not imply fixed-column Eulerian fibers. Historical priority is not independently certified.

value.rationale: Complete all-target residue distribution for every 2^k of a classical permutation statistic, including exact least period and earliest starting index. This goes well beyond existing zero-target divisibility, periodicity upper bounds, or known value tables and supplies a natural inverse-limit Haar isometry structure. A complete natural classification of this infinite family is mathematically meaningful without claiming a downstream grand theorem.
